headline: Energy Leads a Lopsided Session as Healthcare and Chips Draw Heavy Selling
body_html:
Thursday's mid-session tape is decidedly mixed, with 237 stocks rising against 303 falling across our 544-name universe. Energy is the clear pole position, up 1.42% as geopolitical pressure in the Strait of Hormuz pushes oil-supply anxiety to the forefront. Chord Energy, Texas Pacific Land and Valero Energy are each climbing more than 3.9%, reflecting the market's calculus that prolonged Middle East disruption keeps crude prices supported.

The pain is concentrated in Healthcare, off 1.43%, and Semiconductors, sliding 1.41%. argenx is the session's most jarring casualty, tumbling 13.19%, with Glaukos not far behind at -10.97%. MaxLinear and Vicor Corporation are adding to the semiconductor sector's drag. Software is holding a slim 0.51% gain, offering modest counterweight, while Consumer is fractionally positive after Vita Coco surged 5.9% to top the day's leaderboard. GoDaddy's 4.92% advance rounds out the better-received names.

Into the close, traders will be watching the 30-year Treasury auction for any signal on rate direction after the Fed's Waller reiterated a bias toward further hikes. Bond-market volatility has already rattled equity positioning today; another surprise in long-duration demand could swing the final hour sharply. Friday's open will inherit whatever sentiment the auction delivers.

briefs.headline: Hormuz Tension Puts a Bid Under Oil Names Mid-Session
briefs.body: Asia's scramble to stockpile crude and accelerate renewables investment, combined with Iran's pledge to block additional Hormuz shipping lanes, is keeping energy equities elevated. Chord Energy and Valero Energy are among the direct beneficiaries, each posting gains above 3.9% as tanker attack risks climb to wartime highs.

briefs.headline: argenx Leads Healthcare Lower After Sharp Intraday Drop
briefs.body: argenx is off 13.19%, making it the hardest-hit name in the universe so far today, pulling the broader Healthcare sector down 1.43%. Glaukos is also under severe pressure, sliding nearly 11%. The twin declines are dragging on sentiment across biotechnology and medical-device names more broadly.

briefs.headline: Fed's Waller Signals More Hikes; 30-Year Auction in Focus
briefs.body: The 10-year Treasury yield is holding roughly steady after Federal Reserve Governor Waller signaled additional rate increases may be warranted. Options traders have begun positioning for a potential floor in the bond selloff following what sources described as a firm 10-year auction, but the 30-year sale this afternoon remains the key test for the afternoon session.

briefs.headline: Vita Coco Pops to Session High, Pacing the Consumer Group
briefs.body: Vita Coco is the day's standout percentage gainer, rising 5.9% and lifting the Consumer sector to a modest 0.22% advance. The move comes as at least one institutional desk disclosed it is deploying cash into a beaten-down consumer name, suggesting selective accumulation is quietly underway beneath the surface volatility.

briefs.headline: German Growth Upgrade Offers Macro Tailwind for Trade Bulls
briefs.body: Germany's government raised its economic growth projections for both 2026 and 2027, according to Reuters, injecting a degree of optimism into the global macro picture. Separately, the WTO upgraded its forecast for goods trade, crediting the AI-driven demand cycle for partially offsetting disruption stemming from the Middle East conflict.

briefs.headline: GoDaddy Extends Gains as Software Holds Positive Territory
briefs.body: GoDaddy is up 4.92%, the top performer in internet services and a meaningful contributor to the Software sector's 0.51% advance. The gain stands in contrast to the pressure weighing on semiconductor and hardware names, underlining a rotation within the technology complex toward software and services exposure during today's session.
